title: Learn from realised episodes
description: Sample complete episodes, compute discounted returns, and compare MC Basic, Exploring Starts, and ε-greedy control.
ready: Monte Carlo engine ready. Generate an episode to start the ledger.
working: Rust is sampling an episode and updating return means.
failed: The Monte Carlo engine could not start. The static explanation remains available below.
resetDone: The sampled ledger was reset to its initial state.
exploringStartsOff: Use the mode's normal start rule
mapBody: Each cell reports V, the mean return credited to that state; the table below reports Q for each action. Unvisited pairs remain visible, and arrows are the current control policy.
stateValueNote: V is a credited state-return mean; Q rows are the state–action estimates.
episodeEmpty: No episode yet. Generate one to reveal the trajectory.
traceBody: This is the observed path, not a transition-model expansion.
returnBody: Rows show suffix returns and whether the selected initial/first/every-visit rule credited them.
visitCountsBody: Counts are observations, not proof of optimality. The mean and variance are computed from credited returns.
policyProbabilitiesBody: ε-greedy assigns every action a non-zero probability when ε > 0; the other schedules show their deterministic representative.
referenceTitle: What this lab does not claim
referenceBody: There is no exact model reference in this lab. Compare estimates, coverage, and replay metadata instead of treating a finite sample as a Bellman solution.
auditBody: The checks below are derived from realised episodes and the running ledger.
auditModelFree: Updates use realised rewards; no transition table is read
auditNoModel: No model rows are exposed to the learner
auditFinite: Values, counts, probabilities, and returns are finite
auditRows: Every credited return has a matching visit count
auditPolicy: Nonterminal policy probabilities sum to one
auditTrace: The latest trace is internally consistent
errorPrefix: The Monte Carlo engine rejected the command.
staticFallback: If WebAssembly is unavailable, the equations and definitions above remain readable; no sampled value is silently replaced by a model calculation.
